newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares weak on political worries.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares weak on political worries.

text.p: Jordan shares closed lower at the start of weekly trade on Saturday with investor sentiment soured over renewed fears over the fate of Middle East peace, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.33 percent to 152.74 points in business worth 2.13 million dinars ($3 million).
Brokers attributed the market's weakness to renewed worries about the repercussions of a breakdown in the Middle East peace process that could regnite Arab-Israeli bloodshed.

The market, which has traditionally been very senstive to political developments in the region, has recently rebounded sharply by prospects of expanded trade with Baghdad as Iraqi oil once more flowed to world markets.

But uncertainty over how much Jordanian businesses stood to benefit has rattled activity, aborting the market's upward trend since it was announced last month that Iraq was ready to implement the oil-for-food deal.

"Any negative political factor affects the investors psychology and the falls in the market were focused especially on companies linked to the political factor," Mohammed Abdullah, analyst with Pearl Consulting, said.

Turnover was artificially high, dominated by two banks bloc sales, the first by Arab Bank in a deal worth 1,272,900 dinars and another worth 540,000 dinars in 150,000 shares sold in Jordan Investment Finance Bank.

Most leading bluechip fell in across-the-board declines that weighed down on the market despite some select activity and minimal selling pressure that held back the bourse from further declines, brokers said.
Industrial blue-chip Jordan Cement Factories fell 0.08 dinars to 3.45 dinars in minimal 1,480 shares exchanging hands.
Arab Potas, which saw some foreign emerging funds buying last week, remained resilient against the general bearish trend with a 0.05 dinars rise to 5.80 dinars.

Even most of the firms that stand to benefit from Iraq related exports under its oil-for-food deal performed poorly. Blue chip drug firm Arab Pharmarceutical Manufacturers shed 0.06 dinars to 3.60 dinars while Intermediate Petrochemicals lost 0.03 dinars to 1.10 dinars.
Only seven companies rose on Saturday, outnumbered by profit-taking in 21 falling shares. Another three shares were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of 45 best-traded shares shed 0.39 percent 82.51 points, still 13.61 percent down on last year.
